limitations_and_boundaries: CPA will fail if test data are very different from training data; distance-based uncertainty score is implemented to alert users.
Model is based on gene expression alone; cannot capture post-transcriptional modifications, signaling, or cell communication directly.
Predictions cannot replace experimental validation; serve as a guide.
Data uncertainty and biases (e.g., genes co-measured show more complex predictions) may influence model.
Fixed architecture and hyperparameters; systematic sweeping may improve performance.

research_questions.statement: Can a computational model predict single-cell transcriptional responses to unseen combinations of perturbations, dosages, cell types, time points, and species?

claims.statement: CPA can predict held-out perturbation combinations with high accuracy, e.g., R2=0.81 for Panobinostat+Alvespimycin.

provenance.text_excerpt: CPA significantly outperformed scGen on variance prediction by 35.85% improvement and similarly outperformed scGen in whole distribution prediction.

claims.statement: CPA outperforms scGen on variance and distribution prediction, with 35.85% improvement in variance prediction.

methods.name: Compositional Perturbation Autoencoder (CPA)
methods.protocol_description: Autoencoder with factorized latent space: basal state + additive perturbation embeddings + covariate embeddings; adversarial loss for disentanglement; dose-response curves as neural nets; reconstruction loss using Gaussian negative log-likelihood.

methods.name: Training procedure
methods.protocol_description: Optimization of reconstruction, adversarial, and penalty losses; hyperparameters: embedding dimension 256, batch size 128, learning rate 1e-3, etc. (see Table 1).

results.value_raw_text: Including low dosages diminished chemCPA’s performance significantly (Fig 4D).

results.metric_name: R2 score (DEGs) for OOD combination prediction

provenance.text_excerpt: the clear distribution shift induced by the combination of Alvespimycin and Panobinostat (Fig 3A) could not be fully identified by either model, and both models achieved an R2 of about 0.3 on DEGs. In contrast, the other combinations could be predicted with R2 higher than 0.6 for the DEGs in the case of the chemCPA model (Fig 4E).

results.value_raw_text: chemCPA outperformed CPA overall; for Panobinostat+Alvespimycin, both models achieved R2 ~0.3 on DEGs; other combinations predicted with R2 >0.6 for chemCPA (Fig 4E).
